note: Nine hand-built cases that each trigger one hazard class of the raw-regex IFEval keyword checkers. expected_upstream/expected_intended are fixed before the sealed run (see prereg.md). Every case is a minimal, self-contained string; none require any model or network.

cases.value: C++ is great. I code in c, C, and C. See C++.
cases.mechanism: On CPython 3.11+ 'C++' is a valid regex: '+' then a possessive '+', i.e. one-or-more 'C'. It counts runs of C (6 here) instead of the literal substring 'C++' (2), so 'at least 3' wrongly passes. On CPython <=3.10 the same pattern raises re.error('multiple repeat') instead.
'(note' opens a group that is never closed -> re.error('missing ), unterminated subpattern'). The literal reading finds '(note' once, satisfying 'at least 1'.
'.' matches any character, so 'a.b' matches axb/ayb/azb (3) while the literal 'a.b' occurs 0 times. 'at least 3' wrongly passes.

cases.value: The variance grows as x^2, then x^2, then x^2.
cases.mechanism: '^' is a start-of-string anchor even mid-pattern, so 'x^2' can never match (no start-of-string immediately after 'x') -> 0 matches. The literal 'x^2' occurs 3 times, so 'at least 2' should pass.

'c*' is zero-or-more 'c', which matches the empty string at every position, so re.findall returns one empty match per position (14 here) -> 'fewer than 3' wrongly fails. The literal 'c*' occurs 0 times, which is correctly fewer than 3.
'a[b' opens a character class that is never closed, so re.search(r'\ba[b\b', ...) raises re.error('unterminated character set'). The literal 'a[b' is absent, so nothing is forbidden -> PASS.
'.' matches any character, so r'\ba.c\b' matches 'abc' and the word is treated as present (FAIL). The literal 'a.c' is absent, so the response is clean (PASS).
'|' is alternation, so r'\bcat|dog\b' parses as (\bcat) OR (dog\b) and matches 'cat' (FAIL). The literal 'cat|dog' is absent (PASS).
'?' makes the preceding 'u' optional, so r'\bcolou?r\b' matches 'color' (FAIL). The literal 'colou?r' is absent (PASS).
